prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Reform UK “Contract with You” (Manifesto 2024)

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration and stop small boats via detention/deportation and returns to France.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while keeping services free at point of use; tax incentives and use of independent capacity.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; higher rate from £70,000.
- Cut energy bills by scrapping green levies/Net Zero targets; expand UK oil and gas.
- Slash government waste to fund tax cuts and frontline services.

Immigration
- Freeze non-essential immigration; essential health/care skills exempt.
- Leave ECHR; create a Department of Immigration; pick up small boats and return to France.
- Secure detention and rapid processing (offshore if needed); bar asylum/citizenship if arriving from safe countries; no legal aid for non-citizens.
- Immediate deportation for foreign criminals; possible citizenship withdrawal (except minor offences).
- Ban student dependants; restrict post-study stay to essential skills; close fake courses.
- Five-year residency/employment before accessing benefits.
- Employer Immigration Tax: NI at 20% for foreign workers (exempt health/care and smallest firms).

Public spending and tax
- End BoE interest payments on QE reserves.
- Departmental efficiency target: save £5 per £100 spent; cut foreign aid by 50%; strengthen HMRC collection; deregulate retained EU law.
- Personal: lift tax threshold to £20k; reduce fuel duty by 20p; scrap VAT and levies on energy; cut Stamp Duty (0% to £750k, 2% to £1.5m, 4% above); restore VAT-free tourist shopping; IHT: 0% up to £2m, 20% above (charity option).
- Business: raise CT threshold to £100k; cut main CT to 20% then 15%; abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k; abolish business rates for high-street SMEs funded by 4% online delivery tax; deregulate hiring/firing; simplify tax code; fast-track brownfield and infrastructure.

NHS
- Zero basic rate tax for NHS/social care staff for 3 years; end training caps; student loan write-offs tied to service.
- Use independent/not-for-profit capacity (UK/overseas); 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Voucher if GP wait >3 days, consultant >3 weeks, operation >9 weeks.
- Operational efficiencies; expand Pharmacy First; inquiry into excess deaths/vaccine harms.

Energy/Net Zero
- Scrap Net Zero obligations and renewable subsidies (replace with equivalent taxes); fast-track North Sea and shale (with local compensation).
- Expand nuclear SMRs and other technologies.

Policing and justice
- Recruit 40,000 officers over 5 years; zero-tolerance approach; expand stop and search; mandatory prison for knife/violent crimes; life for drug trafficking.
- New leadership standards; cut DE&I roles; de-politicise College of Policing.
- Justice: automatic life for second violent/serious offence; raise budget to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; redefine hate crime; build 10,000 detention places; family court/child grooming/youth training reforms.

Education
- Curriculum review; ban gender transitioning policies in schools; single-sex facilities.
- 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans; longer repayment; minimum entry standards; fewer undergraduate places.
- Enforce free speech in universities; expand PRUs; offer 2-year degrees.

Welfare
- Tougher work requirements (2-strike rule within 4 months); face-to-face assessments; focus on youth employment; apprenticeship tax relief.

Brexit
- Scrap retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate TCA; maintain UK forces’ autonomy.

Defence
- Spend 2.5% GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay review; Armed Forces Justice Bill; new Veterans department; recruit 30,000; procurement and skills reforms.

Housing
- Fast-track brownfield; prioritise locals in social housing; restore mortgage interest relief for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; leasehold protections.

Families
- 25% transferable marriage tax allowance (when affordable); front-load Child Benefit (ages 1–4); single-sex spaces; regulate youth smartphones; review Online Safety Act.

Transport/infrastructure
- Scrap HS2; end ULEZ/LTNs; no ICE bans; improve regional links; new utility ownership model (50% public, 50% UK pensions); cap standing charges; merge infra bodies.

Agriculture and fisheries
- Farm budget to £3bn; end climate-linked subsidies; CMA powers on pricing; “Buy British” targets.
- End automatic foreign access to UK waters; licence/fees; expand patrols; ban supertrawlers/pulse fishing; rebuild processing and fleets.

Pensions/social care
- Royal Commission; curb offshore tax practices in care; pension system review; implement mineworkers’ scheme reforms.

Constitution and governance
- Leave ECHR; reform House of Lords/civil service leadership; restrict postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights.
- Sovereignty and governance reforms (WHO treaty/CBDC positions); replace Equality Act; Free Speech Bill; reform BBC/licence fee; new anti-corruption unit; English/Welsh national holidays.

Costings (party estimates)
- Annual savings: c. £150bn plus £10bn from assumed growth.
- Annual costs: c. £141bn.
